cards.explanation: The answer is finest. The song says he "…planted the finest vines." Not the okay ones, not the leftovers from the clearance rack, friends. I know a thing or two about being picked up cheap, so an owner who goes straight for the best gets my respect. Everything he did for this hill was top shelf.

The answer is a winepress. The verse says he "…dug out a winepress as well." A winepress is where grapes get crushed to make wine, so he's planning for a harvest. Watchtower, finest vines and a winepress, friends: this owner thought of everything.

The answer is sour fruit. The verse says he waited for good grapes, "…but the fruit it produced was sour!" That exclamation point says a lot, friends. After all that digging, planting and building, sour is not what anybody ordered.

The answer is that he asks them to judge between him and his vineyard. The owner says, "…I exhort you to judge between Me and My vineyard." He's talking to the dwellers of Jerusalem and the men of Judah, and he's putting the question in their hands. It's like he sets the whole case in front of them and says, you tell me.

The answer is True. The owner asks, "What more could have been done for My vineyard than I have done for it?" It's a question with nothing left to add, friends. He dug, cleared, planted, built and waited, and then he asks that question.

The answer is that it will be trampled. The owner says, "I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled." A wall is what keeps things out, so once it's down, the vineyard is open to whoever walks through. It's a heavy moment in the song, friends, and I think it's meant to be.

The answer is False. The owner says, "I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor cultivated, and thorns and briers will grow up." No more pruning and no more tending, friends. The song says the opposite of a second try.

The answer is False. The owner says, "I will command the clouds that rain shall not fall on it." That's the last thing he lists, friends, and it's the opposite of pouring rain. Wasteland, thorns and briers, and no rain to follow.

The answer is the LORD of Hosts. Verse 7 says, "For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel…" That's the verse where the song tells us what the vineyard stands for, friends. The vineyard belongs to Him.

The answer is Israel. Verse 7 says, "…the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel…" And the men of Judah are called "…the plant of His delight." Once you know that, friends, every part of the song about the vineyard hits closer to home.

The answer is bloodshed. The verse says, "He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed…" This is a heavy line, friends, and I think it's meant to be. He wanted justice from the plant of His delight and saw bloodshed instead.
